digest.headline: The Nasdaq dropped 975 points as artificial intelligence spending fears triggered a technology selloff.

lede.b: The Nasdaq index, which tracks many large technology companies, fell 975 points to reach a three-month low. This drop happened because investors worried about the high costs and capital expenses needed for artificial intelligence. Capital expenditure refers to the money companies spend to buy or upgrade physical equipment. Intel stock dropped roughly 30% after its third-quarter financial results. Advanced Micro Devices fell 13% and Rigetti Computing shares dropped 75% to hit a new low.
lede.i: The Nasdaq tumbled 975 points to touch a three-month low as investors unwound positions in major technology shares. Widespread fear regarding high financing costs and capital expenditure for artificial intelligence drove the selloff. Intel stock plunged roughly 30% following its third-quarter financial results. Advanced Micro Devices dropped 13% in sympathy with the broader semiconductor slump. Rigetti Computing shares hit a new low after declining 75%.
lede.a: The Nasdaq 100 recorded its third correction of the year as the index dropped 975 points to a near three-month low. Capital expenditure concerns and financing cost pressures for artificial intelligence weighed heavily on semiconductor equities. Intel shares plunged roughly 30% following its third-quarter financial results. Advanced Micro Devices dropped 13% in sympathy, while Rigetti Computing fell 75% to a new low.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Tech stocks slide as AI spending fears grip Nasdaq

stories.t: Nasdaq Drops 975 Points Amid Tech Selloff
stories.b: The Nasdaq is an index, which is a list that tracks the value of a group of technology companies. On this day, the index fell by 975 points. Big technology companies saw their stock prices drop sharply. Stocks are tiny slices of ownership in a business that people buy and sell. Investors panicked because of worries about artificial intelligence spending.
stories.i: The Nasdaq tumbled 975 points to reach a near three-month low. This drop marks the third correction of the year for the Nasdaq 100 as investors unwind positions in major technology shares. Widespread fear regarding capital expenditure and high financing costs for artificial intelligence triggered the selloff.
stories.a: The Nasdaq 100 experienced its third correction of the year, shedding 975 points to hit a three-month low. The sharp retracement underscores a fundamental reassessment of capital expenditure commitments and financing availability for artificial intelligence infrastructure. Markets are now pricing in heightened risks around mega-cap tech valuations as leveraged positions unwind.

stories.t: Chipmaker Shares Plunge Following Earnings Reports
stories.b: Intel shares plunged by about 30% after the company released its third-quarter earnings for 2026. Advanced Micro Devices shares slid by 13% during the same trading session. Rigetti Computing shares hit a new low after enduring a 75% total decline. These sharp drops hurt other major chipmakers across the market.
stories.i: Intel stock plunged roughly 30% following its third-quarter 2026 financial results. Advanced Micro Devices dropped 13% in sympathy with the broader semiconductor slump. Meanwhile, Rigetti Computing shares hit a new low following a 75% decline.
stories.a: Intel shares plummeted approximately 30% on weak third-quarter 2026 metrics, acting as a primary catalyst for the wider chip sector rout. Advanced Micro Devices fell 13% alongside the broader semiconductor liquidation. Rigetti Computing extended its losses, hitting a new low after a cumulative 75% drawdown.

stories.t: Bloom Energy Enters S&P 500 as Federal Reserve Pauses
stories.b: Bloom Energy joined the S&P 500 index, which tracks five hundred large American companies. History shows specific patterns for stocks entering this index. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve decided to pause its policy actions. The Federal Reserve is the central bank of the United States that manages interest rates.
stories.i: Bloom Energy joined the S&P 500 index, prompting analysts to examine historical precedents for newly included equities. Simultaneously, the Federal Reserve implemented a policy pause. This pause highlights the current economic outlook as monitored by businesses like Delta Air Lines.
stories.a: Bloom Energy secured admission to the S&P 500, with market participants evaluating historical valuation trajectories following index inclusion. Concurrently, the Federal Reserve enacted a policy pause. The central bank's stance emphasizes prevailing uncertainties within the macroeconomic outlook.

politics.b: Government officials watched financial markets drop today. Lawmakers focused on the steep losses in technology stocks. Regulators monitored the sharp decline in artificial intelligence investments.
politics.i: Federal authorities monitored the sharp equity correction across technology sectors. Policymakers observed the broader economic signals stemming from the Federal Reserve pause. Officials tracked the market reaction to shifting artificial intelligence expenditures.
politics.a: State actors observed the transmission of tech sector liquidations into broader market volatility. Policymakers assessed macroeconomic signals in light of the Federal Reserve policy pause. Regulatory attention focused on systemic risks arising from concentrated artificial intelligence capital expenditures.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Bank of Japan holds interest rate at 1.25% as Nikkei drops

stories.t: Central Bank Holds Rate Steady as Currency Strengthens
stories.b: The Bank of Japan is the country's central bank, which sets the main borrowing cost for the economy. It decided to keep its policy rate at 1.25%. Following this decision, the Japanese yen gained value against the US dollar. Analysts described the decision as a hawkish hold.
stories.i: The Bank of Japan left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 1.25%. The Japanese currency strengthened against the US dollar following the announcement. Market participants characterized the meeting outcome as a hawkish hold.
stories.a: The Bank of Japan maintained its policy rate at 1.25%. The currency appreciated against the dollar in response to the perceived hawkish hold. Implied pricing indicates continued focus on potential future policy normalisation paths.

stories.t: Nikkei Falls 3% Amid Global Technology Selloff
stories.b: The Nikkei is an index, which is a basket of major company shares that tracks how the stock market is performing. It dropped 1,369 points to close at 63,290. This decline was driven by a drop in chip stocks and doubts over spending on artificial intelligence following losses on the Nasdaq index.
stories.i: The Nikkei 225 index tumbled 1,369 points to finish at 63,290, recording a 3% drop. Semiconductor equities retreated as artificial intelligence spending doubts spread from the Nasdaq index. Afternoon trading sessions featured volatile price swings.
stories.a: The Nikkei 225 declined 3% or 1,369 points to close at 63,290. Technology shares faced broad liquidation following weaker sentiment on the Nasdaq index. Chip equities absorbed the primary impact as artificial intelligence infrastructure expenditure concerns weighed on valuations.

stories.t: Murata Commits $6.3 Billion to Artificial Intelligence Capacitors
stories.b: Murata is a Japanese manufacturing company that makes electronic components. It announced a plan to spend $6.3bn over five years. The money will build new production facilities for capacitors used in artificial intelligence technology.
stories.i: Murata announced a $6.3bn capital expenditure plan spanning five years. The funding targets increased production capacity for capacitors driven by artificial intelligence demand. Semiconductor component suppliers continue expanding output to meet tech sector requirements.
stories.a: Murata committed $6.3bn over a five-year horizon to expand capacitor manufacturing facilities. The investment addresses structurally higher demand derived from artificial intelligence hardware deployments. Component producers scale capital expenditure programmes despite broader macroeconomic uncertainty.

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI auctions, bank rates and six-month market highs

stories.t: State and Treasury Debt Auctions
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India runs auctions where the government borrows money by selling short-term debt called Treasury bills. Think of a Treasury bill like a short-term IOU where investors lend cash to the government and get it back later with a small bonus. The bank scheduled sales worth 23,000 Crore rupees across different maturities for early November 2026. State governments also offered to raise 29,900 Crore rupees through separate stock auctions.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled debt auctions totaling 23,000 Crore rupees across 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day Treasury bills for settlement in November 2026. State governments simultaneously offered to raise 29,900 Crore rupees through separate stock auctions, featuring re-issued securities such as the 7.46% Andhra Pradesh SGS 2035. These borrowing operations form part of routine sovereign debt management.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India announced a 23,000 Crore rupee issuance across 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day Treasury bills alongside 29,900 Crore rupees in state government securities auctions. State issuance includes re-issued paper such as the 7.46% Andhra Pradesh SGS 2035 and 7.81% paper carrying greenshoe options. These concurrent sovereign and sub-sovereign auctions test primary dealer absorption capacity at the short and medium ends of the yield curve.

stories.t: Commercial Bank Lending Rates Hold Steady
stories.b: Scheduled commercial banks in India kept their average lending rates unchanged. The weighted average lending rate on outstanding rupee loans stayed at 8.96% in September 2026. This figure remained the same as the previous month. This average tracks the actual interest that borrowers pay across all outstanding loans from these banks.
stories.i: Scheduled commercial banks maintained their weighted average lending rate on outstanding rupee loans at 8.96% through September 2026, recording no change from August 2026. Data covering lending and deposit rates of scheduled commercial banks excludes regional rural banks and small finance banks. This metric captures the actual composite borrowing cost across the existing loan book of the banking sector.
stories.a: Scheduled commercial banks reported an unchanged weighted average lending rate of 8.96% on outstanding rupee loans for September 2026 relative to August 2026, excluding regional rural banks and small finance banks. The stagnant composite rate reflects sticky legacy pricing across the broader credit portfolio despite shifting interbank liquidity conditions. Transmission from policy rates to the outstanding credit book remains muted as banks defend deposit margins.

stories.t: Equities Reach Six-Month Peaks
stories.b: Stock markets in India climbed to a six-month high in October 2026. Rallies in technology stocks and enthusiasm around initial public offerings helped drive the gains. The Sensex index gained 300 points during one session as foreign buying increased. At the same time, the Indian rupee rose against the US dollar.
stories.i: Indian stock markets touched a six-month high in October 2026 driven by rallies in technology shares and initial public offering activity involving firms such as Jio Platforms. The Sensex gained 300 points in a single session amid renewed foreign institutional buying. Concurrently, the rupee appreciated 50 paise to reach 94.76 against the US dollar.
stories.a: Indian equities reached a six-month peak in October 2026 underpinned by technology sector rallies and primary market demand from initial public offerings like Jio Platforms. The Sensex advanced 300 points over consecutive sessions supported by foreign portfolio inflows and domestic buying. Meanwhile, the rupee appreciated 50 paise to close at 94.76 against the US dollar despite lingering petroleum supply risks.

politics.i: The Central Board of the Reserve Bank of India convened its 625th meeting in Mumbai chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra. Directors participated in the Integrity Pledge as part of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 observations. The board reviewed prevailing macroeconomic indicators and assessed systemic risk profiles.

stories.b: Petrobras finishes drilling the Morpho well in block FZA-M-59. This marks the third oil find in that area. The company also opens a tender for biomethane. Traders balance these new exploration wins against a softening market for oil.
stories.i: Petrobras concludes drilling operations at the Morpho well within block FZA-M-59, confirming a third pay zone. The energy firm also launches a biomethane tender while navigating a softer crude tape. Traders weigh these exploration discoveries against broader commodity headwinds.
stories.a: Petrobras completes Morpho drilling in block FZA-M-59, validating a third hydrocarbon column in ultra-deep waters off Amapá. Concurrently, the state-controlled operator opens a biomethane tender amid a softening oil tape. Market participants reconcile these upstream additions with weaker benchmark crude pricing.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Aramco pricing shifts and security updates

stories.t: Aramco Adjusts Pricing and Output Capacities
stories.b: Saudi Aramco is the state-owned oil company of Saudi Arabia, which is a massive business that pumps crude oil from the ground and sells it globally. The company cut its official selling price for Arab Light oil destined for Asia by the largest margin in over twenty years. At the same time, the chief executive officer stated that the firm can make 12 million barrels per day available within days if required.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco reduced its official selling price for Arab Light crude to Asia by the largest drop in over two decades. Concurrently, the firm's chief executive officer stated that output capacity of 12 million barrels per day can be made available within days. These adjustments accompany moves to raise liquefied petroleum gas prices for November alongside Sonatrach.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco implemented its largest price cut in over two decades for Arab Light crude destined for Asia. Management concurrently asserted that 12 million barrels per day of productive capacity remains accessible within days. These pricing adjustments coincide with parallel increases in November liquefied petroleum gas official selling prices set alongside Sonatrach.

stories.t: Security Incidents and Infrastructure Updates
stories.b: A drone attack was intercepted near the Shaybah oilfield operated by Saudi Aramco, resulting in two deaths. Meanwhile, the chief executive officer warned that the global oil stockpile could take two years to rebuild after the Strait of Hormuz reopens. The company also announced plans to partner with various countries to expand its oil storage footprint.
stories.i: Two individuals were killed after a drone was intercepted near Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield. The firm's chief executive officer warned that rebuilding global crude stockpiles could require two years following the reopening of Hormuz. Management also pursued international partnerships to expand physical oil storage infrastructure.
stories.a: A fatal drone interception occurred near Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, claiming two lives. Executive leadership subsequently warned that rebuilding aggregate petroleum stockpiles post-Hormuz reopening could span a two-year horizon. Concurrently, corporate strategy involves establishing bilateral partnerships with consuming nations to decentralize and expand oil reserve storage.

politics.a: Qatari diplomatic delegations rotated back to Tehran with an updated framework proposal intended to terminate the regional conflict. Bilateral talks persist via intermediary channels as state actors attempt to de-escalate active hostilities.

stories.b: The country's pool of foreign money has grown to $55.26bn. This growth helped the local currency, the naira, to rise in value against foreign money. Currency traders watch these reserves because higher totals give the central bank more ability to support the money supply.
stories.i: The national external reserves climbed to $55.26bn, providing support that allowed the naira to gain strength in currency trading. Higher reserve balances typically expand the central bank's capacity to intervene in foreign exchange markets.
stories.a: External reserves expanded to $55.26bn, bolstering the naira's spot valuation through improved reserve adequacy metrics. This liquidity buffer reduces immediate pressures on foreign exchange auctions managed by monetary authorities.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Aussie Dollar rises on rate hike bets and hot inflation

stories.t: Australian Dollar and Interest Rates
stories.b: The Australian Dollar went up after a hot inflation report came out. Inflation is when prices rise and money buys less. People now think the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates. Interest rates are the cost of borrowing money. The currency held steady at first before climbing.
stories.i: The Australian Dollar edged higher as markets priced in a greater probability of a Reserve Bank of Australia rate hike following a hot inflation print. Traders adjusted rate expectations after consumer price data exceeded forecasts, complicating the central bank's policy path. The currency maintained stability initially before extending gains.
stories.a: The Australian currency nudged higher as hotter-than-expected inflation prints catalyzed a repricing of Reserve Bank of Australia terminal rate expectations. Forward curves steepened as sticky price pressures, complicated further by volatile travel components, forced desks to re-evaluate the probability of tightening. The cross maintained its bid structure ahead of concurrent Federal Reserve decisions.

stories.t: Healthcare Stocks and Economic Pressures
stories.b: Healthcare shares on the Australian stock exchange went up. They rose even though economic headwinds cast a spooky shadow over the market. Scott Power reported on these movements in The Mercury. The gains happened while broader economic pressures worried investors.
stories.i: Healthcare equities on the ASX advanced despite broader economic headwinds weighing on sentiment. Analyst Scott Power noted the resilience within the healthcare sector amid challenging macroeconomic conditions. These stock movements occurred alongside general market uncertainty.
stories.a: ASX healthcare equities posted gains despite mounting macroeconomic headwinds acting as a drag on risk assets. Sector participants navigated persistent cost pressures while maintaining relative outperformance against cyclical indices. These valuations reflect idiosyncratic sector resilience rather than broad macro tailwinds.
